aspects.says: Adding a checked exception to a method's throws clause breaks every caller's source unless it was already handled through a supertype; adding an unchecked one breaks nothing.
basis: section:Adding a Checked Exception Breaks Every Caller's Source; Adding an Unchecked One Breaks None

aspects.says: A catch for Exception does not catch a checked Throwable that is not an Exception.
basis: section:A Throwable Is Checked Unless It Is a RuntimeException or an Error

aspects.says: Every Throwable is checked except RuntimeException, Error and their subclasses, so a class extending Throwable directly is checked.
basis: section:A Throwable Is Checked Unless It Is a RuntimeException or an Error

aspects.says: An exception is checked when the caller can act on it and couldn't prevent it, unchecked when it means a bug; the same failure can be either depending on where the input comes from.
basis: section:Make It Checked When the Caller Can Act on It, Unchecked When It Means a Bug

aspects.says: A checked exception added to an interface method breaks calls through the interface but not implementations; an implementation can't add one the interface lacks.
basis: section:Adding a Checked Exception Breaks Every Caller's Source; Adding an Unchecked One Breaks None

aspects.says: The JVM doesn't check throws clauses, so code compiled against an older library receives checked exceptions it never declared, past a catch for RuntimeException.
basis: section:Catch-or-Declare Is a Compiler Rule; at Run Time Any Method Can Throw a Checked Exception

aspects.says: At run time checked and unchecked exceptions are thrown, caught and cost the same.
basis: section:Catch-or-Declare Is a Compiler Rule; at Run Time Any Method Can Throw a Checked Exception

aspects.says: Class.newInstance passes a constructor's checked exception on unwrapped; Constructor.newInstance wraps it in InvocationTargetException.
basis: section:Catch-or-Declare Is a Compiler Rule; at Run Time Any Method Can Throw a Checked Exception
aspects.reason: it is the behaviour of a deprecated JDK method shown by a run; a practice would only re-run the JDK

aspects.says: Removing a checked exception from a method makes callers' catch clauses for it fail to compile.
basis: section:Adding a Checked Exception Breaks Every Caller's Source; Adding an Unchecked One Breaks None
aspects.reason: a compile error javac enforces: no wrong solution compiles, so there is nothing a graded test can catch, and unit 3.1.2's practice already grades the never-thrown catch

aspects.says: Files.lines and BufferedReader.lines throw read errors as UncheckedIOException from the terminal operation, past a catch for IOException; unwrapping getCause() restores the IOException.
basis: section:Streams Can't Throw IOException, So Files.lines Throws UncheckedIOException from the Terminal Operation
